data.name: Hint
data.value: If the company uses part of your home as its office, it can rent that part from you, unfurnished, under a lease. It pays the rent out of its profit, before your pay, and deducts it. The rent is never pay: you are taxed on it with your pay, on less than the rent and without social contributions.

data.name: CadastralIncomeHint
data.value: Not indexed, as your property-tax notice or MyMinfin gives it.

data.name: ShareHint
data.value: The part of your home the company uses, usually by floor area.

data.name: Help_Cap
data.value: At most {0} for the year: 5/3 of {1}, the cadastral income of the part let, revalued by {2}. Above it, the excess would be taxed as director pay.

data.name: Help_CadastralIncome
data.value: The notional yearly rental income the administration sets for a property, on which its property tax is computed.

data.name: Help_Floor
data.value: The rent is under the floor, so you are taxed on the floor: the cadastral income of the part let, indexed, plus 40%.

data.name: Help_FlatCharges
data.value: A flat deduction for maintenance and repairs in place of real costs: a share of the rent, capped by the revalued cadastral income of the part let.

data.name: Remove
data.value: Remove home office rent from your plan
